note_tweet.text:
Privacy in the Age of AI - Is Privacy truly dead?

Unbelievable in less than a year we've gone from OpenClaw to now multiple personal AI agent platforms namely - Grokbot, OpenAI Dots, Meta Muse and Google Gemini/Spark just to name a few.

In order for these to be useful you need to feed it info, they are very data hungry and it's the "context" paired with the power of AI that makes them so useful.

But what happens when they start harvesting more data than what you thought?

Meta's Muse builds and maintains detailed “pages” or profiles on friends, family, colleagues, partners, and others mentioned in those communications—even people who never signed up for Muse or consented to any data sharing. These profiles can include relationship history, preferences, shared interests, and other details extracted from emails, chats, contacts, and photos. Muse is instructed to update them roughly hourly using the user’s data (plus public information).

I'd argue this extends surveillance to non-consenting third parties: your consent covers your data, but not the information about others sitting in your inbox or messages. Meta’s response is that this context is needed for the agent to be useful which is probably true.

Interestingly from my quick research, none of the other personal agent platforms go to this level of data harvesting. The cynic in me thinks this is what happens when your personal agent is built by a company who's business is to sell advertising. But the practical implication is Meta is right, the more data you give your personal agent the more useful it will be.

So what's it going to be?

note_tweet.text:
Sarvam just plugged its Indus agents into Figma through MCP. Here's what you need to know.

Sarvam announced that agents built on its Indus model can now create designs directly in Figma. They read your components, variables and layouts, then build with them inside the file. Sarvam posted the news on Oct 16, 2026.

It ties to Figma's first-ever Config India, held Oct 15, 2026 at BIEC in Bengaluru. Figma announced 20 new MCP partners there, and Sarvam Agents is one of them. Figma also announced an MCP partnership with Sarvam as part of its largest investment in India yet.

The other partners on the list: Amp, ClickUp, Dia, Junie by JetBrains, Linear, Meta Muse, Mistral, Notion, OpenCode, Agentforce Vibes, Amazon Quick, Amplitude Wave, Cline, Delta, Dust, Glass, Gradial, Writer, Zed and Microsoft 365 Copilot.

Figma also launched new ways to build with code on the canvas. That includes code layers, Figma Specs as a native home for context, and connections to a backend framework and a CMS for real data and content.

Figma also shared a survey of 507 Indian respondents. AI adoption in design is rising and product-building workflows are getting faster. The same people worry that AI-generated output looks generic.

Reactions from the event were mixed. Attendees praised the energy and the crowds of designers. One said the show felt underwhelming and the queues were long. Another pointed to a line heard on stage, "We're not here to replace anybody, we're just here to increase productivity." One developer said writebacks that change shared variables should need human approval.

Key numbers:
- 20 new MCP partners announced
- 507 survey responses from India
- Oct 15, 2026: first Config India, Bengaluru

Sarvam's Indus agents can now read and build with a team's own Figma design system.

Spotify doesn't actually expose their music recommendation engine via their API, and that's why I had to bring https://t.co/fR0HbAQ88n into it, and at first I thought that would be a show stopper, but Gus, my Meta Muse knocked it out of the park and got everything working and set up.

We had to do some correction to build a routine that can crawl through songs using the https://t.co/fR0HbAQ88n data to find related tracks to build playlists, and I also gave it a fun 70's Funky Disco look at the end.  This was a super fun build and it just makes me more and more grateful for our AI tools every day.  This would have been such a hassle to make in 2024
